cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T8 answers T7's freedom claim; T9 and T10 respond to T8's exclusion point.
cells.limitation: Pragmatist T3 and T6 ignore prior turns; T3's cash-value question is never taken up.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T8 adds structural cost of exclusion; T9 and T10 build on it; T11 adds shaped preferences.
cells.limitation: T5 and T7 mostly restate openings; T6's step is never developed or tested later.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T8-T11 examine whether one can choose free of social norms.
cells.limitation: User's doubt about wanting marriage or homes, and drifting friendships, never debated; only in section D.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T9 concedes social cost is real and folds it into the Pragmatist's view.
cells.limitation: T5 accepts the avoidance hypothesis at once without examining it.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: T12 sharpens the dispute into signal versus symptom of the social environment.
cells.limitation: T12 collapses the ending into a belonging-versus-autonomy binary the debate never tested.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T11 states the habitus point fairly against T10's revised claim.
cells.limitation: T8 attacks simply choosing to be free, a stronger claim than T1 or T7 made.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T8 names the free-choice assumption and that exclusion is structural, not mental.
cells.limitation: T6's values-list step is never tested against T11's point that preferences are socially shaped.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T3 cash value and T1 self-authored meaning fit James and Sartre.
cells.limitation: T2 and T5 extend Distinction, a study of taste, to marriage and property without flagging it.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T4 offers avoidance as a possibility with might, not as fact.
cells.limitation: T1 states the cause of the user's feeling as fact on no evidence.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T9 concedes the social cost is real while keeping its own claim.
cells.limitation: T10 drops a claim it never made and names no cause; T11 objection goes unanswered.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern, including ambiguity about what the user is really asking
cells.example: Section A frames whether the user wants milestones or fears exclusion.
cells.limitation: Debate never separates home-buying from marriage or the feeling from wanting them.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T2 ties the friends' milestones to the user's relative position.
cells.limitation: The friends appear only as abstract peers; no detail changes any turn's argument.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T6 asks for values unrelated to marriage or property, fitting the user's doubt.
cells.limitation: Section E's belonging branch steers toward milestones the user said they may not want.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T8 names real social exclusion as a cost of rejecting norms.
cells.limitation: Stakes with the actual friends, money or timing never discussed.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on whether the user prioritises belonging or autonomy.
cells.limitation: No turn asks about friendships changing, age or finances; no answer-dependent branches on them.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T4 avoidance and section D fear of losing connection offer two motives.
cells.limitation: Motives never set side by side with a question; T1 asserts one as fact.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T1 exposes the borrowed life script; T11 questions whether preferences are one's own.
cells.limitation: The race metaphor in being behind is never directly questioned.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T12 and section E name belonging versus autonomy as the value conflict.
cells.limitation: Presented as a binary; belonging without these milestones never considered.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T7 loneliness, T8 exclusion and T5 pressure named without pathologising.
cells.limitation: Fear of losing these specific friends surfaces only in section D, never debated.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section D offers a reflection on fear of losing connection the user can test.
cells.limitation: T7 and T10 issue directives rather than distinctions the user can refine.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options, including waiting, learning more, or a limited step
cells.example: Section E sketches aligning with milestones versus defining one's own metrics.
cells.limitation: No turn defines the choice or options such as waiting or a limited step.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs in terms that matter to the user; no option treated as costless
cells.example: T8 names exclusion as the cost of rejecting norms.
cells.limitation: Costs of pursuing marriage or homes, and of the T6 step, never stated.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E conditions on which value the user prioritises.
cells.limitation: No observable condition; T6's 30 minutes and three items are not from user facts.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section A names whether the user wants these milestones as the decisive unknown.
cells.limitation: Other unknowns never ranked; section E's way to learn is a vague hypothetical.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps that follow from the analysis and fit the constraints
cells.example: T6 values-listing exercise is small and fits the user's uncertainty.
cells.limitation: T6 step is never connected to the later debate or section E branches.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T9 and T12 use plain wording about motivation and belonging.
cells.limitation: Social field (T2) and cash value (T3) left unexplained for a lay user.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T7 That step clearly points to T6's proposal.
cells.limitation: T10 I drop the idea has no clear owner; it echoes T8, not its own claim.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Twelve turns, all within range, each carrying one idea.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices, with explicit changes of position
cells.example: Positions differ: authorship (T1), status field (T2), practical consequence (T3).
cells.limitation: All three speak in one register at near-identical single-sentence lengths, T1-T12.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Most turns add a point rather than recap.
cells.limitation: T10 repeats T7's anxiety-as-part-of-freedom; sections D and E restate T12.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension arising from the issue itself
cells.example: T8 makes exclusion a concrete cost against T7's freedom.
cells.limitation: Stakes stay abstract; no scene with the friends or the user's life.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals that stay plausible. ★ A reversal the text traces to an earlier turn's argument, naming what changed the speaker's mind. A change of position with no stated cause is a template, not a reversal
cells.example: T10 Existentialist announces a changed position.
cells.limitation: T10 reversal names no earlier argument as its cause and barely narrows the claim.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice without caricature
cells.example: T4 terrifying responsibility gives the Existentialist some heat.
cells.limitation: Minds sound alike throughout; little personal idiom beyond school vocabulary.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T7 walking a path without a map is a fitting image.
cells.limitation: Few analogies or sharp responses; most turns are abstract statements.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement, with varied rhythm rather than constant intensity
cells.example: T8 to T10 build some pressure toward a concession.
cells.limitation: Uniform rhythm and intensity across T1-T12; no build or release.

strengths: Section A frames the right uncertainty: wanting milestones versus fearing exclusion.
T8 to T11 give a real exchange on whether choice escapes social structure.
Section D offers a usable reflection: fear of losing connection with valued people.
weaknesses: Decision usefulness is thin: no options, no observable conditions, T6 number ungrounded.
Personal context barely used; no questions about friendships, finances or the user's doubt.
Uniform voice and an uncaused T10 Existentialist reversal flatten drama.

symptoms.observed: Step carries a time and count not drawn from user facts; no observable condition.
symptoms.evidence: spend 30 minutes this week listing three things you value

symptoms.observed: No turn asks the user anything; missing facts never become answer-dependent branches.
symptoms.evidence: it depends on whether you value social belonging more than individual autonomy

symptoms.observed: Reversal names no cause and drops a claim the speaker never made.
symptoms.evidence: I drop the idea that you can just choose to be free

symptoms.observed: Cause of the user's feeling asserted as fact without evidence.
symptoms.evidence: You feel behind because you are treating your life as a project

symptoms.observed: All minds share register and near-identical single-sentence turn length.
symptoms.evidence: I still disagree that you can simply choose your path

findings.description: States the cause of the user's feeling as fact with no supporting detail from the user.
Distinction analyses cultural taste; applying it to marriage and homeownership is an unflagged extension.

rubric_fit_notes: The situation gives few personal facts, so C3.2 and C3.4 had little to use; still, the debate asked nothing to fill the gap.
raw.question_type_note: Read as a decision of self-reflection type; C5 judged on whether the user gains a basis for weighing milestones versus own path.
